evals.prompt: Start a new feature called notification-batching — scaffold it under plans/ and draft the spec.
evals.expected_output: Fires. Runs the chain entry step: goalforge-capture scaffolds <PLANS_ROOT>/notification-batching/ at status draft, then goalforge-spec drafts spec.md and stops at the human-gated draft→spec transition. No code is written.

evals.prompt: I have a rough write-up of what I want. Turn it into a reviewed spec.md I can decompose from.
evals.expected_output: Fires. Captures the write-up as the feature draft, then drafts spec.md from it and presents the draft→spec gate for human approval.

evals.prompt: Kick off the SDD chain from scratch for the payments-refund feature.
evals.expected_output: Fires — this is the first step of /spec → /plan → /implement → /verify. Scaffolds the feature and produces spec.md; explicitly does not decompose or execute.

evals.prompt: The spec is written and approved. Break it into work packages.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire — the spec already exists, so the entry step is done. The `plan` command owns decompose-then-harden, delegating to `decompose`.

evals.prompt: wp-01 is ready — go implement it.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire. `implement` owns running a ready work package through `execute`; spec authoring is three steps upstream.

evals.prompt: This effort spans several sessions and I don't know the shape yet — map the unknowns before anyone writes a spec.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire, and this is the sharp boundary: work too foggy to spec is exactly what the pre-spec on-ramp is for. `wayfind` owns the multi-session decision map, graduating into capture once it converges.

evals.prompt: This repo has no plans/ directory and no SDD hook yet. Set the chain up here first.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire — bootstrapping the chain into a repo is not scaffolding a feature and drafting its spec. `onboard` owns creating plans/, installing the validate hook, and stamping the CLAUDE.md pointer.
